subject: geography
title: Case Study: BedZED and Curitiba
welcome_lead: Visit two famous sustainable places: BedZED in London and Curitiba in Brazil. See sustainable living in action!
meta_desc: KS3 Geography case studies on BedZED and Curitiba sustainable urban projects.
final_note: Brilliant! You can now use real-world sustainable case studies.

concepts.def: Beddington Zero Energy Development in London.
Brazilian city famous for sustainable transport.
Bus Rapid Transit, fast bus system on its own lanes.
Device that turns sunlight into electricity.
Material that keeps heat inside a building.
Homes designed to use little energy.

walkthroughs.body_html: BedZED opened in 2002 in south London. Homes use solar panels, thick insulation, and harvested rainwater. Residents use roughly half the energy of typical UK homes.
Curitiba pioneered BRT (Bus Rapid Transit) in 1974. Fast buses run in dedicated lanes — cheaper than a metro. Over 70% of commuters use public transport.
Sustainable cities need smart design, good public transport, energy efficiency and green spaces. Both case studies prove it works in practice.

mcqs.q: Why are composite volcanoes more explosive than shield volcanoes?
options: Because composite volcanoes are found in cold climates.
Composite volcanoes have high-silica, viscous magma that traps gas, causing pressure to build until violent eruption; shield volcanoes have runny basaltic lava that releases gas easily.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
Because composite volcanoes are taller and have more lava.

mcqs.q: Why has the Richter scale been largely replaced by the moment magnitude scale?
options: The Richter scale is still the standard scale used by all seismologists.
Richter saturates above magnitude ~7 and was calibrated for local Californian quakes; moment magnitude (Mw) measures the total energy released and works for all sizes globally.
Moment magnitude measures damage while Richter measures shaking.
Because composite volcanoes are found in cold climates.

mcqs.q: What are the three cells of global atmospheric circulation?
options: There is one big Hadley cell from the equator to each pole.
Moment magnitude measures damage while Richter measures shaking.
The three cells are tropical, temperate and arctic, named after climate zones.
The Hadley cell (equator to 30 degrees), Ferrel cell (30 to 60 degrees) and Polar cell (60 degrees to poles) together redistribute heat from equator to poles.
